User.title: User
User.description: Represents a unique device-based user of the LifeOS application. This entity stores user-specific settings and metadata without requiring login credentials.

id.description: Unique identifier for the User entity, typically corresponding to a device ID.

createdAt.description: Timestamp indicating when the user's record was first created.

passcodeEnabled.description: A flag indicating whether the app's passcode lock feature is enabled for this user.

Habit.title: Habit
Habit.description: Manages individual habits a user tracks, including their current streak and completion status.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Habit entity.

userId.description: Reference to the User who owns this habit. (Relationship: User 1:N Habit)

title.description: The name or description of the habit.

streak.description: The current number of consecutive days the habit has been maintained.

lastCompleted.description: The date and time when the habit was last marked as completed.

status.description: The current status of the habit (e.g., 'active', 'paused', 'completed').

Task.title: Task
Task.description: Stores individual tasks and their associated details, allowing users to manage their to-do list.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Task entity.

userId.description: Reference to the User who owns this task. (Relationship: User 1:N Task)

title.description: The name or description of the task.

status.description: The current completion status of the task (e.g., 'pending', 'in-progress', 'completed').

project.description: The project or category this task belongs to. (Note: treated as a simple string as per schema, not a foreign key to a 'Project' entity).

dueDate.description: The deadline for completing the task.

Challenge.title: Challenge
Challenge.description: Represents a gamified challenge a user is participating in, tracking their progress over a defined period.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Challenge entity.

userId.description: Reference to the User who is undertaking this challenge. (Relationship: User 1:N Challenge)

title.description: The name or description of the challenge.

currentDay.description: The current day of progress within the challenge.

totalDays.description: The total number of days planned for the challenge.

FitnessRecord.title: FitnessRecord
FitnessRecord.description: Captures daily or session-based fitness activity data for a user.

id.description: Unique identifier for the FitnessRecord entity.

userId.description: Reference to the User whose fitness activity is being recorded. (Relationship: User 1:N FitnessRecord)

date.description: The date when the fitness activity occurred.

steps.description: The number of steps taken during the activity.

distance.description: The distance covered during the activity, typically in kilometers or miles.

time.description: The duration of the fitness activity, typically in minutes or hours.

FinanceTransaction.title: FinanceTransaction
FinanceTransaction.description: Records individual financial transactions (expenses or income) for a user.

id.description: Unique identifier for the FinanceTransaction entity.

userId.description: Reference to the User who made this transaction. (Relationship: User 1:N FinanceTransaction)

amount.description: The monetary amount of the transaction.

category.description: The category the transaction belongs to (e.g., 'food', 'transport', 'bills').

date.description: The date when the transaction occurred.

StudyProgress.title: StudyProgress
StudyProgress.description: Tracks a user's progress in various study subjects or courses.

id.description: Unique identifier for the StudyProgress entity.

userId.description: Reference to the User whose study progress is being tracked. (Relationship: User 1:N StudyProgress)

subject.description: The name of the study subject or topic.

progress.description: The current progress percentage or level in the subject.

firestore.reasoning:
The Firestore structure is designed following the core principles of Authorization Independence, Structural Segregation, and Access Modeling, specifically tailored for a device-based, single-user application without explicit login.

**Authorization Independence (CRITICAL):**
All user-specific data (Habits, Tasks, Challenges, Fitness, Finance, Study) are stored in subcollections directly under a user's dedicated document: `/users/{userId}/<collectionName>/{documentId}`. This hierarchical structure ensures that the `userId` in the path segment directly dictates ownership and access permissions. For example, `/users/{userId}/habits/{habitId}` clearly indicates that `habitId` belongs to `userId`. This design eliminates the need for `get()` calls in Firestore Security Rules to check parent document attributes for authorization. Rules can simply compare `request.auth.uid` (which is assumed to be the `device_id` from Firebase Anonymous Authentication, mapping to `userId` in the path) directly against the `{userId}` wildcard in the path. This makes authorization atomic, efficient, and robust, as there are no cross-document dependencies.

**Support for QAPs (Queries as Permissions):**
By strictly segregating each user's data under their respective `userId` document, `list` queries inherently comply with security rules. When a client requests `/users/{request.auth.uid}/habits`, the rules will ensure that only documents where the path's `{userId}` matches `request.auth.uid` are returned. This prevents clients from inadvertently or maliciously querying data belonging to other users, as unauthorized queries would simply yield no results or be denied by the rules. The database structure itself acts as a strong access control mechanism, fulfilling the QAP principle.

**Structural Segregation & Access Modeling:**
Each logical entity (Habit, Task, etc.) gets its own subcollection under the user's document, ensuring that all documents within a given subcollection (`/users/{userId}/habits`) share the same security posture (owned by `userId`). This uses the 'Path-Based Ownership' and 'Hierarchical Paths for User-Owned Data' models, which are highly secure and simplify rule writing. The `userId` field is also explicitly included within each document of the subcollections, serving as a denormalized field for data integrity and query flexibility, even though the path is the primary authorization enforcer for security rules. This radical consistency ensures that the data's intent and ownership are always clear.
